subject: Intermittent API pulse — EntropyWave customer bulletin
messages:
From: Redwood Platform Ops <ops@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Ops] Brief: short-lived API pulse observed (investigating)

Team —

We observed short, intermittent drops in request throughput to the hosted inference API across a small subset of customers beginning ~08:58 PST. The behavior looks like a rapid "pulse" of elevated 5xx and cancelled streams that resolves within ~20–45s per occurrence but recurred three times in the 08:58–09:05 window.

Initial findings:
- Kernel saturations on a small pool of us-west serving machines coincident with large streaming sessions (p99 sequence lengths spiked).
- Automatic routing fallback prevented broader pool impact, but a subset of requests were routed rather than queued and saw brief failures.
- No onboarding config changes recorded during the window.

Action taken so far:
- Increased routing backfill and temporarily diverted new streaming sessions to a warm pool.
- Kicked an ops runbook to collect KV cache stats, kernel metrics, and full request traces.

I'll follow up with a customer-facing blurb for affected customers once we confirm the scope.

—Ravi (on-call)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@entropywave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent API pulse — EntropyWave customer bulletin

Hi Elena —

Wanted to let you know proactively that we saw a brief, intermittent interruption affecting streaming generation for a small number of hosts this morning (8:58–09:05 PST window). Your team’s traffic hit the affected cohort for two short pulses and some requests returned 502/stream-cancel errors during those spikes.

What happened (summary):
- Short, repeated throughput drops in a us-west serving pool tied to unusual long-sequence streaming sessions.
- Automatic fallback and rerouting reduced blast radius, but a subset of sessions experienced a ~20–45 second failure before recovery.

What we did for EntropyWave: 
- Diverted new streaming sessions to a warmed reserve pool for immediate stability.
- Prioritized request traces for your top-traffic API keys and captured KV/cache state.
- Created ticket RDW-4521 to track customer impact and follow-up items.

Current status:
- The platform is stable; no ongoing pulses after 09:10 PST.
- We published a short incident entry on our status page (link below) and are preparing a post-incident summary.

Links & artifacts:
- Incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-12-22-entropy-pulse
- Support ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/ticket/RDW-4521
- Attached: incident-log-20261222.txt (ops traces), customer-impact-summary.pdf

If you saw production errors or missed events that matter for your SLA or user experience, please reply with the time windows and we’ll include that in the impact assessment. We’re also happy to schedule a short sync today if you prefer to walk through traces.

Sorry for the interruption — we’ll share a short postmortem once the team finishes root cause analysis.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@entropywave.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@entropywave.ai
Date: 2026-12-22 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent API pulse — EntropyWave customer bulletin

Thanks for the heads-up, Lukas. We did see a spike of failed generation events in our observability around 08:59 and again at 09:03 PST; a handful of user-facing sessions retried and eventually succeeded, but we lost consistency for a short window and a couple of background jobs timed out.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether any inference requests were duplicated or returned partial payloads during the pulses? We have strict idempotency expectations for a couple of batch jobs.
2) If there are any mitigation steps we should take on our side (client retry/backoff configs, connection windows), please list them.

We appreciate the quick reroute. A 30-minute sync today would be helpful for the engineering leads to review traces. We’re flexible after 13:00 PST.

—Elena
Director, Platform Engineering, EntropyWave

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@entropywave.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent API pulse — EntropyWave customer bulletin

Hi Elena —

Thanks for confirming what you observed. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) Duplicates / partial payloads:
- Our traces show increased 502s and cancellations; we did not see duplicated complete responses tied to the pulses. There are a small number of partially streamed responses that were cancelled mid-stream — those are not full payloads and we flagged them as errors in the ticket. We will include exact request-ids in the ticket for your team to map.

2) Mitigation guidance (client side):
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter for streaming session establishment failures.
- Treat cancelled/502 during streaming as non-idempotent — do not auto-supersede without server-side confirmation.
- For long-running jobs, implement a short checkpointing approach if possible (persist intermediate outputs).

What we will deliver:
- A compact post-incident summary (root cause hypothesis, timeline, scope, and remediation) by EOD.
- A list of request-ids that touched your API keys for the 08:55–09:10 window so your team can reconcile.
- Follow-up action: kernel selection logic patch to reduce saturation risk; we’ll propose a controlled rollout and a configuration flag you can opt into.

Would 13:30 PST work for a 30-minute sync? I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the incident artifacts so we can walk traces with your engineers.

Apologies again for the disruption — appreciate the quick heads-up from your side.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
